ai.summary: The SDK now provisions a pinned Node.js build for sponsored runs that lack a host installation, addressing the `missing_node` failure mode where advertiser procedures requiring `npx` could not start. A new module, `sponsored-managed-node.ts`, downloads Node `v24.21.0` from nodejs.org, verifies its SHA-256 checksum, and unpacks it into `~/.freebuff/toolchains/` with a `.freebuff-verified` marker to ensure atomicity. The `createSponsoredTerminalBroker` function in `sponsored-sandbox.ts` was updated to accept a `managedToolchains` option, granting the toolchain root as a read-only source and appending its `bin` directory to the end of the run's `PATH` so user-installed Node versions take precedence.
ai.evidence: The diff adds `sdk/src/tools/sponsored-managed-node.ts`, which exports `ensureSponsoredManagedNode` and `SPONSORED_MANAGED_NODE_VERSION` ('v24.21.0'), and modifies `sdk/src/tools/sponsored-sandbox.ts` to add a `managedToolchains` option to `SponsoredSandboxOptions` and update `createSponsoredTerminalBroker` to append managed bin directories to `PATH` and their roots to `additionalReadRoots`.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show which specific CLI or Desktop components call `ensureSponsoredManagedNode` and pass the result to `createSponsoredTerminalBroker`, leaving the exact integration point within the run lifecycle unconfirmed.

eli5.text: The developer kit for the coding assistant can now automatically download and install a safe, read-only version of the Node.js runtime on your computer if it is missing. This specifically helps sponsored tasks that need Node.js to run commands, preventing failures on machines where the tool was not previously set up. If the download fails, the task simply proceeds without the extra runtime as it would have before, so you face no new action or visible change in daily use.
